text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.3% today after oil prices dropped following diplomatic signals from Iran's leadership about potential conditions to end the conflict. This comes just a day after the stock jumped 3.8% on Middle East supply concerns from Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries — the reversal reflects investors stepping back from crisis-premium bets as peace talks appear to gain traction. The broader picture matters here: the stock is still up 5% over two weeks, showing that despite today's pullback, energy traders remain positioned for higher prices amid ongoing regional tensions.

The price swings also reflect competing currents in how traders view oil supply risk. While the Trump administration's reported willingness to allow more Russian diesel onto the market suggests some supply relief ahead, most analysts don't expect that to meaningfully lower prices given the small volume involved — meaning the market remains focused on what happens with Iran and Middle East production instead.
